start.text: Lina Zhao. I run a cross-border payments startup; Nexus lets me hold office hours here. Let me guess: you paid a supplier abroad and the money hasn't landed.
Wires go through a chain of correspondent banks. Right now every bank in that chain is double-checking everything.
You have three ways to pay abroad now.
A wire: cheap, slow. A letter of credit: we guarantee you to their bank, about two days, one and a half percent.
Or digital dollars through a licensed exchange. Minutes, tiny fee. But you're trusting the platform, not a bank.

choices.text: Set me up with a digital dollar account.

digital.text: Sensible to have both. The exchange has to verify you first. It takes a few hours.
Know who you're paying, and know who's holding your money in between. That's the whole job now.

lc.text: Boring and safe. My favourite. You'll find it when you pay Lumina: Company OS, Operations.

later.text: Take your time. The ships certainly are.

on_end.text: Your exchange account is verified. Digital dollars are an option when you pay abroad now.
